**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

I use to bunk classes to sneak in the (1)/ library and most of my class notebooks (2)/ were filled with poems and essays. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The above sentence is in past tense. It can be seen by the use of **‘were**’ in the third part of the sentence.

So, the first part of the sentence is in present tense making **option 1** as the correct answer to mark the error.

Thus, the verb **‘use**’ should be changed from present tense to past tense by replacing it with ‘**used**’.

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Which very much is (1)/ trying to fit round pegs (2)/ in square holes. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "1"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "which very much is" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "which is very much"
 
• According to grammar, adverbs/adverbial phrases are generally used in between the auxiliary verb and the main verb. In the given sentence, "very much" is an adverbial phrase hence, we need to use this phrase in between "is" and "trying"

**So the correct sentence is- ***Which is **very much** trying to fit round pegs in square holes.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

We will not want our kids (1)/to be influenced by (2)/such TV serials. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. We will not want our kids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase '**We will not want**' is incorrect as it does not fit the context.
 
• The correct way to express this idea is '**We do not want**'.
 
• Using '**do not**' conveys a present, ongoing concern rather than a future requirement.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: ***We do not want our kids** to be influenced by such TV serials.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In negative constructions expressing a general preference or desire, 'do not' (for present) or 'will not' (for future) should be used correctly according to the context.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternatives which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.**

Of course some of the most important **(uses for water)** are at out homes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Uses of water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The preposition 'of' is followed by a noun (water) expressing the object of the verb (uses) underlying the first noun.
 
• The preposition ‘**for**’, on the other hand, initially came from ‘**before’**, which also means ‘**on the account of**’.

Thus, in the above sentence, the bracketed part of the sentence can be improved by replacing it with **option 1, **i.e., ‘**Uses of Water**’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternatives which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.**

You are enjoying the thrill **(of the mid-week holiday)** but I’m here to change that.
questions.solution:
The definite article ‘**the’ **refers to some specific object or some specific person. An indefinite article ‘**a**’ and ‘**an**’ refers to a non-specific object or person. Both articles must be followed by a noun or an adjective and a noun.

While ‘**the**’ can be used for singular or plural nouns, ‘**a’** and ‘**an**’ are used only for singular nouns.

Thus, in the above sentence, the bracketed part of the sentence can be improved by replacing it with **option 3, **i.e., ‘**Of a mid-week holiday**’ because holiday is mentioned in the sentence making it singular.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Taj Mahal is one of ______ greatest wonders of the world.
questions.solution:
The above sentence includes a superlative adjective, ‘**greatest**’.

The structure of a sentence having a superlative adjective is:

**Noun (subject) + verb + the + superlative adjective + noun (object).**

Thus, ‘**the**’ or **option 3** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

If Shruti had worked hard she ______ got the job.
questions.solution:
The above sentence is in past perfect tense, which could be identified by the structure of past perfect tense as seen in the sentence:

Main verb: **Past participle (3rd form of the verb) i.e., worked**

Auxiliary verb: **Had**

As the sentence includes ‘**if**’ in the sentence it shows a certain possibility of an event in the upcoming future, while the sentence is in past perfect tense, thus, ‘**would have**’ or **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Kapil ______ to cinema every Monday evening
questions.solution:
The above sentence is in present simple tense.

We use the simple present tense when an action is happening right now, or when it happens regularly (or unceasingly, which is why it's sometimes called present indefinite). Depending on the person, the simple present tense is formed by using the root form or by adding ‑s or ‑es to the end.

Thus, first form of the verb would be used as a main verb in the sentence making **option 2** as the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

All the

P: come under the public sector

Q: government-owned

R: production units
questions.solution:
The first part of the sentence should initiate the topic of the sentence.

Out of P, Q, and R:

P and R are incomplete as P doesn’t tell what **comes under the public sector; **R doesn’t tell **what production units are talked about.**

Thus, making **Q** the** first part** of the sentence.

The second part of the sentence should complete the meaning of the first part of the sentence.

Out of P and R:

P is still dependent on the meaning of the sentence as it doesn’t make sense to link **government-owned** with **come under the public sector.**

The link between them is **R **which completes the sentence as it tells production units are owned by the government making **R **as the **second part** of the sentence and remaining **P **as the **third part** of the sentence.

Thus, **QRP** or **option 1** is the correct answer.

Thus, making **P **as the** second part** and **Q** as the** third part** of the sentence.

We are left with **R** which makes the first part of the sentence.

Thus, **RPQ** or **option 4** is the correct answer.

The second part of the sentence must include emergence due to global warming as in the first part of the sentence, the last word arising which means emerge.

The part which includes the emergence is **R** as it links **arising** with **out of** making it as the second part of the sentence.

Thus, making **P** as the third part of the sentence.

Hence, **QRP** or **option 4** is the correct answer.

Even a poor peasant

P: happier than the rich

Q: with good health is

R: person with poor health
questions.solution:
The first part of the sentence should relate to **a poor peasant.**

Out of the options mentioned above,

**P **and **R **relate to each other as **P** ends with ‘**the rich**’ while **R** starts with ‘**person**’ making them relatable and, thus, making them as the second and third part of the sentence.

While

**Q** relates to the poor peasant regarding his good health making it as the **first part** of the sentence.

Thus, **QPR** or **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

The cashier took the money from the customer.

options.text: The money is taken from the customer by the cashier.
The money was taken from the customer by the cashier.
The customer was taken the money by the cashier.
The money had been taken from the customer by the cashier.

questions.solution:
The above sentence is in active voice. The structure of a sentence with active voice is:

**Subject (cashier) + Verb (take) + Object (money)**

To convert it into passive voice, the structure must be reversed. Thus, reversing the structure would make **option 2** as the correct answer.

questions.question:

The rules to change interrogative sentence into passive voice are:

Change the** subject** into **object.**

Change the **object** into** subject.**

Use **past participle **form of the verb.

Use ‘**by**’ with object.

Use **auxiliary verb** at the beginning of a sentence.

Thus, making **option 2 **as the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Ramesh said to me, “where have you been last night?”

options.text: Ramesh asked me where had I been the previous night.
Ramesh asked me where I have been the previous night.
Ramesh asked me where I am the previous night.
Ramesh asked me where I had been the previous night.

questions.solution:
The above question is in **direct speech** and is in** present perfect tense**.

Present perfect tense combines the present tense and the perfect aspect used to express an event that happened in the past that has present consequences.

To change present perfect tense into indirect speech, the sentence must be changed into **past perfect tense.**

Thus, ‘**have’** changes into ‘**had’,** making **option 4** as the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“I’m taking my kid to the zoo tomorrow,” he said, “to see the baby tiger.”

options.text: He said that he will take the kid to the zoo to see the baby tiger tomorrow.
He said that he would take the kid to the zoo the next day to see the baby tiger.
He said that he was taking his kid to the zoo the next day to see the baby tiger.
He said that he was taking the kid to the zoo that day to see the baby tiger.

questions.solution:
The above sentence is in **direct speech**, and is in** present continuous tense** for future arrangements.

**The present continuous tense is formed from the present tense of the verb be and the present participle (-ing form) of a verb.**

To change present continuous tense into indirect speech, the sentence must be changed into **past continuous tense.**

Thus, ‘**am’** changes into** ‘was’**, making **option 3** as the correct answer.

Thus, ‘**today’** becomes ‘**that day’** making **option 3** as the correct answer.

questions.question: What happened when Chopin moved to Cloutierville?

options.text: She gained insight on local culture.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Her husband died unexpectedly."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• When you read the passage you will find the following lines:
 
 
• Kate Chopin was born in St. Louis, Missouri, in 1850, one of the five children but the only one to live through her twenties. Her father, Thomas O’Flaherty died when she was five, and she spent her childhood among women: her mother, Eliza; grandmother; great-grandmother; and the nuns who ran her school. In 1870, **Chopin married Oscar Chopin** and moved with him to New Orleans, where they had six children. Chopin was an independent spirit who smoked cigarettes, walked alone through the city, and argued passionately with others about politics and social problems, much to the dismay of the other New Orleans housewives in her social circle. **Not long after the family moved to Cloutierville, Louisiana, Oscar died unexpectedly.** Chopin mourned his death deeply but eventually embraced her independence, even going so far as to having an affair with a married man. Chopin soon returned to St. Louis, where she would spend the rest of her life. She published her first novel, At Fault, in 1890, when she was forty. The novel was well received, and she went on to publish short stories and essays addressing similar topics. She published two collections of short stories, Bayou Folk (1894) and A Night in Arcadia (1897) and became known as a writer with a keen eye for local culture. “The Story of an Hour” was published in 1894 and, along with “The Storm” (1898), is among Chopin’s most famous stories. Although Chopin’s female protagonists act in unconventional, even scandalous ways, readers accepted this as a simple part of the storytelling and didn’t suspect Chopin of moralising or trying to insert her personal opinions into her work.​
 
 
 
• **The first bold statement says Oscar was her husband.**
 
• **The second bold statement says Oscar died after they moved to Coutierville.**

Hence, the correct answer** **is** "option 3"**
